title: Sidney Bechet's summers with Duke and his cab story
summary: Duke played summer gigs in New England for Si Scribner with Bechet, Carney and Braud, and Bechet explained two days missing by claiming he fell asleep in a cab.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: During the period we were talking about in New York, it was somewhere around in there, was it not, that Sidney Bechet worked very briefly with Dukes Land this man?

Yeah, he worked -- See, Duke used to play a summer gig for a guy named Si Scribner in the New England states, and Sidney, he used to work with Duke -- Sidney -- and they'd go up there for about -- well, the Bubber summer months. Harry Carney and Bechet and Bubba and Braud.

And during that time, that period, Sidney was drinking heavy -- well, Sidney still drank heavy until he died. But one time he was telling us a story that they hadn't seen Sidney for two days and finally on the third night here comes Sidney. So Duke started to ask him, "Where have you been?" He said, "You won't believe this, but I was in a cab and fell asleep and I just woke up and here I am here." And everybody had to break up laughing because it was such a funny story, a lie.
